title: Hyb-Learn: A Framework for On-Device Self-Supervised Continual Learning with Hybrid RRAM/SRAM Memory
problem: RRAM-based on-device training suffers from high energy consumption during weight reprogramming and limited cell endurance. Continual learning systems experience catastrophic forgetting when sequentially acquiring knowledge from multiple tasks.
motivation: Enabling efficient on-device continual learning on edge devices preserves privacy and eliminates data transmission while allowing models to adapt to new tasks without forgetting prior knowledge.
method: Hyb-Learn partitions the neural network into two groups based on task-correlated PE-wise correlation: frozen weights with strong task correlation are stored in RRAM to eliminate reprogramming costs, while trainable weights are stored in SRAM. Self-supervised learning initialized from a pre-trained model trains new tasks while maximizing the freezing ratio to improve efficiency.
key_novelty: First framework enabling on-device continual learning by mapping task-correlated frozen weights to RRAM and updatable weights to SRAM, eliminating high RRAM reprogramming costs while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
contributions: First on-device continual learning framework with hybrid RRAM/SRAM IMC architecture
Task-correlated PE-wise correlation method to intelligently partition and freeze weights across memory types
Self-supervised learning approach to maximize freezing ratio while maintaining accuracy
Solution addressing catastrophic forgetting in RRAM-based continual learning systems

metrics.other: training efficiency improved, freezing ratio maximized

limitations: Specific experimental results, scalability to large models, and comparison with other continual learning approaches not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: On-device continual learning with hybrid RRAM/SRAM architecture
